messages:
megan_support: Hey team, multiple customers reporting 502/504s on hosted inference in eu2 (az2) starting ~08:10 UTC. AcmeCo called in and has a repro. RequestID sample: req_0a1b2c3d. Can we triage? :rotating_light:
lia_oncall: ack. I'm on it. Can you paste one full request id + approximate timestamps? :eyes:
megan_support: AcmeCo, region eu2/az2. Sample req: req_0a1b2c3d at 2026-03-17T08:12:47Z. Support logs show gateway 502 and increased latency (>2s) for some calls. Repro with curl: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.com (10.20.30.40) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< {"error":"upstream unavailable"}
```
tom_network: I'm seeing BGP withdraws to upstream provider AS64501 in eu2 around 08:09-08:14 with multiple short flaps. Egress packet loss to that provider spiking to ~15% in az2. Sharing traceroute/tcpdump snippets to incident channel. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
anna_prod_sre: Edge LB healthchecks show 503/timeout to a subset of model nodes in az2. Retransmits and socket timeouts increased. Failover to other AZ didn't trigger because of existing route stickiness for warm connections. Escalating to P0. :rotating_light:
rahul_eng: Runtime telemetry: token p95 jumped 220ms -> 1.8s for requests touching az2 at 08:10. Request queue depth up, some grpc streams timing out. KV cache hit rates unchanged, so not model-level. Looks TCP-level.
EdgeBot: Alert: eu2/az2 upstream-loss spike detected, 502 rate +400% in 5m. New incident INC-2026-4882 created.
opsbot: Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/network-egress-flap (routing mitigations, BGP guidance, customer comms checklist)
charlie_support: Customer on call wants ETA. Any immediate mitigation we can offer them to reduce errors? Suggest failover to eu1 or dedicated?
lia_oncall: Mitigations suggested: 1) temporarily prefer alternate upstream provider (prov-B) for eu2 egress (manual BGP prepends). 2) increase LB healthcheck aggressiveness to evict flapping nodes. 3) offer affected customers a manual region failover (eu1) for short term. I'm applying 1 now.
tom_network: Confirmed: Prov-A (AS64501) is showing route withdraws and rapid AS path changes. Network applied local prepends to prefer Prov-B route. BGP table changes pushed at 08:18 UTC. Monitoring for convergence.
megan_support: Routing change applied by oncall. AcmeCo reports partial recovery (some 200s) at 08:21 UTC. Sending them a short update.
rahul_eng: After reroute we see initial drop in 502s but a small tail of retries persists. Increased edge request timeout from 10s -> 15s for in-flight to avoid mid-flight drops while downstream converges.
anna_prod_sre: Post-mitigation summary: 502/504 rate in az2 down ~85% vs peak. Healthchecks stabilizing, node eviction completed. Keeping incident open for monitoring and postmortem.
megan_support: Thanks. Drafting customer note: "We're routing around an upstream provider issue affecting eu2/az2; services partially restored and we're monitoring. We're investigating root cause and will follow up." Any other lines to include?
lia_oncall: Add: "If you see further failures, please include requestID and timestamps; short retries (10-15s) often succeed during convergence." Also note alternative region option. :thumbsup:
tom_network: I'll file a ticket with the upstream provider (ASN 64501) with pcap/traceroute artifacts and ask for root-cause. Provider ETA 2-4 hours per initial response.
EdgeBot: Incident INC-2026-4882 status -> mitigated (monitoring).
charlie_support: Customer acknowledged and changed status to partial-recovery. They appreciate the update and will reopen if it recurs.
lia_oncall: Assigning postmortem to network + runtime teams. Suspected provider-side MPLS micro-reorder / transient blackhole causing TCP stalls and reorders leading to upstream 502s. Tagging @tom_network @anna_prod_sre for RCA. Will keep monitoring until 09:00 UTC then handoff to follow-up oncall.
megan_support: Closing loop with customer. Thanks all.
